draft.title: The Linnaean hierarchy
card: The Linnaean system sorts living things into groups that sit inside bigger groups. The levels are kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species.
Kingdom is the biggest group and species is the smallest. Each step down gives a smaller group with fewer organisms in it.
Organisms in the same group share features. The lower the level, the more features they share, so two organisms in the same family have more in common than two in the same class.
A memory trick for the order is: King Philip Came Over For Good Soup. Each word starts with the same letter as a level.
draft.remember: Going down from kingdom to species, groups get smaller and their members share more features.

a.q: Two animals are in the same order but different families. Which pair of animals shares the most features with each other?
opts: Two animals in the same genus
Two animals in the same class
Two animals in the same phylum
Two animals in the same kingdom
a.why: Genus is a lower level than order, so animals in the same genus share more features than animals grouped only at order or above. Animals in the same kingdom share the fewest, because kingdom is the biggest group.
a.clue: Lower levels have smaller groups with more in common.

b.q: A scientist sorts a beetle into these groups: family, class, genus, order. Which list puts them from the biggest group to the smallest?
opts: Class, order, family, genus
Order, class, genus, family
Genus, family, order, class
Class, family, order, genus
b.why: The levels go class, order, family, genus from biggest to smallest, with each step holding fewer organisms. Genus, family, order, class is the reverse, so it runs from smallest to biggest.
b.clue: Start with the level closest to kingdom.

a.best: Two animals in the same genus

problems.detail: The opening sentence ('Two animals are in the same order but different families') has nothing to do with the question or the options, which compare new pairs. Students may try to fit those two animals into the answer and get confused. Remove it, or rewrite the question so it uses that pair.

check.summary: The card and both answers are correct. Question a opens with a sentence about two animals in the same order but different families that the options never use, which could confuse students and should be removed.
